# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 1
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 1

---

*[The world is divided. Thomas gets India. And promptly refuses.]*

1. We were all in Jerusalem at that time — the whole company of apostles: Simon Peter and Andrew his brother, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax-collector, James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananean, and Judas Iscariot. We cast lots to divide the world, so that each of us would go to his appointed region and bring the message he had received.

2. The lot fell to Judas Thomas — also known as Didymus, the Twin — and his region was India.

3. He refused. "I don't have the strength," he said. "I'm not well. And besides — I am a Hebrew. How am I supposed to walk into India and preach the truth to Indians?"

4. While he was still arguing, the Lord appeared to him in a dream that night. "Don't be afraid, Thomas," the Lord said. "Go to India. Preach. My grace will go with you."

5. Thomas still refused. "Send me anywhere you want," he said. "But not India."

6. While all this was going on, a merchant from India happened to be in the city. His name was Abbanes, and he had been sent by King Gundaphorus with a specific commission: find a skilled carpenter and bring him back.

7. The Lord spotted him in the marketplace. "Are you looking to buy a carpenter?" he said.

8. "I am," Abbanes said.

9. "I have a slave," the Lord said, "a carpenter. I want to sell him." And he pointed toward Thomas from across the marketplace.

10. They struck a deal: three litrae of uncoined silver. And they put it in writing. The document read: "I, Jesus, son of Joseph the carpenter, of Bethlehem in Judaea, hereby sell my slave — name of Judas — to you, Abbanes, merchant in the service of Gundaphorus, King of India."

11. When the papers were complete, the Lord brought Thomas to Abbanes.

12. Abbanes looked at him. "Is this man your master?" he asked.

13. "Yes," Thomas said. "He is my Lord."

14. "Then I've bought you from him," Abbanes said. And Thomas said nothing.

---
*PNEUMA note: The Acts of Thomas opens with divine comedy — the apostle of India wants to be anywhere but India, and God sells him there. The bill of sale (v.10) is one of the strangest documents in all of Christian literature: Jesus Christ, son of Joseph, carpenter of Bethlehem, vendor. Thomas's silence at the end (v.14) is the moment of surrender. The man who refused has been purchased.*
